summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted after his tunneled central line spontaneously displaced, interrupting his continuous remodulin infusion for portopulmonary hypertension. He was stabilized with a peripheral IV remodulin infusion and underwent urgent placement of a new right internal jugular tunneled catheter, which was successfully implanted with the tip in the right atrium. He tolerated the procedure well without complications. His chronic conditions, including cirrhosis, ascites, thrombocytopenia, and vertebral compression fractures, remained stable. He resumed his home remodulin dose through the new line and was discharged home the following day with instructions to monitor weight, manage his line, and follow up with transplant clinic. No new infections or procedural complications occurred.
